Tex. proceeding between these parties was found. The venue discrepancy and inability to verify the reporter citation leave this unverifiable within the 3-search budget.

35 U.S.C. §112 is a well-established statutory provision in U.S. patent law (written description and enablement), codified in Title 35 of the United States Code. The citation exactly identifies this statute by its standard statutory reference; no authors or year are required for a U.S. Code provision. LII and related sources confirm its existence.

The case "Polaris PowerLED Technologies, LLC v. Samsung Electronics America, Inc." exists as a real federal patent case filed in the Eastern District of Texas (No. 2:2022cv00469). The cited name matches with only a minor capitalization difference ("Powerled" vs "PowerLED"), which is a trivial transcription variant that does not change which case is being cited.

The case Polaris PowerLED Technologies, LLC v. Samsung Electronics America, Inc. exists as No. 2:2017cv00715 (E.D. Tex. 2019), decided in the Eastern District of Texas, not the Northern District as cited. The case name, year, and approximate reporter volume (386 F. Supp. 3d) match; the venue abbreviation "N.D. Tex." vs. the correct "E.D. Tex." is a transcription error that does not change which case is being cited.

No study titled "Ferinject in Acute Myocardial Infarction (FAIR) study" exists in The Lancet or anywhere on the open web. The FAIR acronym in the literature belongs to FAIR-HF (Ferinject Assessment in patients with Iron deficiency and chronic Heart Failure), a chronic heart failure trial, not an AMI trial. The Ferinject/Lancet/2020 intersection points to AFFIRM-AHF, which studied acute heart failure, not acute myocardial infarction. The cited title and framing do not match any real work.

The real paper is "The European guideline on management of major bleeding and coagulopathy following trauma: fifth edition" by Spahn, Bouillon, Cerny et al., published in Critical Care 2019, DOI 10.1186/s13054-019-2347-3. The citation has a slightly paraphrased title and incorrect DOI (10.1186/s13054-019-2407-3 vs the real 10.1186/s13054-019-2347-3), but the first-author surname, coauthors, year, and venue all unambiguously identify this real work, making this a metadata-error case that falls under REAL per the taxonomy.

No matching paper with the cited title and venue can be found on the open web.

The cited DOI and page range found no corroborating references anywhere on the open web, indicating a fabricated citation.

The cited title and author pair do not correspond to any real publication.

Cheney v. United States District Court for the District of Columbia, 542 U.S. 367 (2004) is a real U.S. Supreme Court case, confirmed via Justia, Wikipedia, Oyez, Cornell LII, Library of Congress, and CourtListener. The case name, reporter citation, and year exactly match the official record.

Three WebSearch queries (title+authors+year; authors+venue+year; author's broader publication list) found no work titled "Love, Sex, and Migration: The Intimate Lives of Young Cross-Border Migrants in Urban Chiang Mai, Thailand" by Powdthavee and Chaiwutthana anywhere on the open web, nor any Culture, Health & Sexuality 2018 paper matching this byline.
